intention: make boundary-guard passes clean with zero escape hatches: the gateway no longer names internal/telemetry, and gets its battery-history data from internal/analytics, which already owns the table.
request: Source ticket MAG-41 — fix the boundary-guard violation. Analyze which DB table the gateway reads through internal/telemetry and move that read to the module the owner picks. Owner picked internal/analytics.

decisions.what: internal/analytics owns the battery-history read, not a gateway-local interface over telemetry.
decisions.why: analytics already owns vehicle_metrics and already serves the two sibling history charts. A local interface would satisfy the guard's letter while keeping the runtime dependency the guard exists to stop.

decisions.what: New method BatteryLevelByDay on the existing analytics.Reader returning []DayBattery — not a new port, not a new type family.
decisions.why: Mirrors ConsumedByDay/OdometerDeltaByDay exactly and completes the existing DayConsumption/DayDistance vocabulary, so an agent looks the pattern up instead of re-inventing it.
metric_date is already the effective day, so the port returns exactly [start,end]. The lookback only ever compensated for the captured_at to EffectiveDate conversion the raw snapshot read needed.

decisions.what: Accept and document the vehicle_metrics vs vehicle_snapshots day-coverage gap; do not add a backfill tier.
decisions.why: A day with no metric row renders as the existing empty no-snapshot bar. Coverage tracks snapshots 1:1 modulo the recalculator watermark, so the effect is bounded to a recent day briefly showing empty.

decisions.what: No new unit tests. Repair the two gateway test files whose telemetry-typed fakes stop compiling.
decisions.why: Owner's standing default is no new tests, but the fake rework is repair required to keep the suite compiling — not new coverage.

decisions.what: The database design gate is recorded as not tripped: no table, column, index, constraint, view or migration changes.
decisions.why: All three needed columns are original NOT NULL columns, and the existing UNIQUE (account_id, tesla_id, metric_date) index already serves the query. The only new artifact is a SELECT.
